Cock-a-Leekie Soup

Served at: Burns Night Supper

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Cock-a-Leekie Soup is a traditional Scottish dish often served at Burns Night Suppers, celebrating the life and poetry of Robert Burns. This hearty, comforting soup combines chicken and leeks with prunes for a subtle sweetness, embodying the rustic flavors of Scotland.

Ingredients

  • 1 whole chicken (about 3-4 lbs / 1.4-1.8 kg)
  • 8 cups (1.9 L) water
  • 4 large leeks, white and light green parts only, sliced and rinsed well
  • 1 cup (150 g) pitted prunes
  • 2 medium carrots, peeled and sliced
  • 2 celery stalks, sliced
  • 1 small onion, peeled and halved
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 6 whole black peppercorns
  • Salt to taste
  • Freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • Chopped fresh parsley for garnish

Method

  1. Place the whole chicken in a large stockpot and cover with 8 cups (1.9 L) of water.
  2. Add the onion, bay leaves, and black peppercorns to the pot.
  3. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a simmer and cook uncovered for about 1 hour, skimming off any foam that rises to the surface.
  4. Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside to cool.
  5. Add the sliced leeks, carrots, celery, and prunes to the broth.
  6. Simmer the soup for another 30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
  7. While the soup simmers, remove the skin and bones from the chicken and shred the meat into bite-sized pieces.
  8. Return the shredded chicken to the soup, season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste, and heat through for 5 minutes.
  9. Remove bay leaves before serving.
  10. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

Tips

  • Use a whole chicken with bones for a richer, more flavorful broth.
  • If prunes are not preferred, dried apricots can be used for a different sweet note.
  • Serve with traditional Scottish oatcakes or crusty bread for a complete Burns Night meal.
